newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kobe Kiito to disband Brazilian unit, sell land.
newsitem.headline: Kobe Kiito to disband Brazilian unit, sell land.

text.p: Kobe Kiito Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it would disband its Brazilian unit and sell part of its landholdings in western Japan, but added this would have almost no bearing on its projected earnings.

The textiles and silk yarn company said it had decided to disband Kobes do Brasil Industria e Comercio Ltda some time in calendar 1997 due to the sluggish silk industry and the Brazilian currency's rise against the dollar.
Kobe Kiito also said that it had decided to sell part of the land it owned in Kobe, western Japan, to the Construction Ministry in late March.
The company said it expected a profit of 1.05 billion yen from the land sale.
Kobe Kiito, however, said that the decisions would have virtually no impact on its projected earnings for the year to December 31, 1997.
Last week, the company said it expected its 1997 parent current profit to be 80 million yen, compared with an actual 1996 current profit of 32 million yen.
